key_big: |x − c| is the distance from x to c.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • g(x) = a|b(x − c)| + d has its vertex at (c, d). A negative a opens down.
  • |x − c| is the distance from x to c. “Within d” means |x − c| ≤ d.
  • |A| = k (k > 0) gives two equations: A = k or A = −k. |A| = negative has no solution.
  • |A| < k: −k < A < k (and). |A| > k: A < −k or A > k (or).

Examples

Example

|2x − 3| ≤ 7

−7 ≤ 2x − 3 ≤ 7

−4 ≤ 2x ≤ 10

Answer: −2 ≤ x ≤ 5

Example

Within 4 of 70

Distance from 70 is |t − 70|

Answer: |t − 70| ≤ 4

Solving only one case|x − 2| = 5 gives 7 and −3.
Using and for >|x| > 3 means x < −3 or x > 3.

items.q: Describe how the graph of g(x) = |x − 4| + 2 is related to the graph of the parent function f(x) = |x|.
items.e: Inside the function, (x − 4) moves the graph the opposite way: right 4. Outside, +2 moves it up. Shift right 4, up 2.

items.q: Describe how the graph of g(x) = |x + 6| − 5 is related to the graph of the parent function f(x) = |x|.
items.e: Inside the function, (x + 6) moves the graph the opposite way: left 6. Outside, −5 moves it down. Shift left 6, down 5.

items.q: The point (2, 2) is on the graph of f(x) = |x|. Which point is on the graph of g(x) = |12x|?
items.e: g(4) = f(12 · 4) = f(2) = 2. Divide the x-coordinate by 12 and keep the y-coordinate. (4, 2).

items.q: The point (−6, 6) is on the graph of f(x) = |x|. Which point is on the graph of g(x) = |12x|?
items.e: g(−12) = f(12 · −12) = f(−6) = 6. Divide the x-coordinate by 12 and keep the y-coordinate. (−12, 6).
